record.one_liner: Shared-inbox and customer communication platform for email, SMS, chat and other channels, with a Core API for messages, contacts, inboxes and analytics.
record.auth_notes: Two Bearer-token routes: API tokens created by a company admin in settings, or OAuth for public/partner integrations. OAuth is preferred for public integrations.
record.access_notes: critic: access paid_plan -> self_serve_trial. No free plan, but a free 14-day trial gives Professional-plan access and an admin can create API tokens; the API is not gated to a specific tier (rate limits 50/100/200 rpm on Starter/Professional/Enterprise). Ongoing use needs a paid seat.
record.api_notes: Core API covers messages, contacts, channels, inboxes, teammates and analytics, with webhooks. Plugin SDK and Channel API are separate. critic: api_style rest confirmed; replaced unverifiable evidence with the authentication page showing the api2.frontapp.com REST endpoint.
record.blocker_notes: critic: verdict blocked -> ready, blocker paid_plan -> none. A free trial issues working API credentials and the API is available on every paid plan including Starter, so there is no approval, sales or tier gate; only a paid seat for ongoing use.

evidence.quote: There are two ways to get a Bearer token — through API tokens in your settings or through an OAuth implementation.
You must be a Front company admin to manage API tokens.
When you start a free 14-day trial of Front, you'll have access to the Professional plan, which includes certain limitations.
By default, Front's API rate limit starts at 50 requests per minute and varies depending on your plan.
The Core API uses Bearer tokens to authenticate its user.
The Core API is Front’s “backend” API that allows developers to access and update almost all elements in Front
Front's MCP server lets you and your teammates connect Front to AI assistants like Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Microsoft Copilot.
Rate limit increases beyond the default limits require the Professional plan or higher.
